verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the implementation-relevant acceptance condition that model figures and their derivation must be understandable and easy to follow.
First concrete failure: the client reports being unable to follow the figures or determine how they were generated.
The client adds an implementation-relevant structural direction to use a simpler model approach; no existing attribute becomes obsolete.
The client adds auditability as a concrete acceptance condition for the revised financial model; no prior value requires removal.
The source presents an unresolved, materially different choice between fully visible driver-level detail and a concise front-facing summary backed by hidden detail.
Post-revision persistence: the client reports that the delivered material remains difficult to understand after repeated revisions and rejects it for a rebuild.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports completing a substantially reworked second version intended to make the model easier to review.
